newsitem.title: GERMANY: Supply tightens in Bremen cotton market.
newsitem.headline: Supply tightens in Bremen cotton market.

text.p: European cotton consumers are seeking nearby raw material but old crop supplies from Central Asia, West Africa and Greece are declining, the Bremen Cotton Exchange said in a market report.
Argentina and Paraguay were also unable to supply cotton from their new harvests.
Origin offers from 1997/98 new crops were scarce and expensive.
A lower estimate for the 1997/98 U.S. harvest from the USDA supported dollar-denominated upland prices.
Buyers exploited dollar dips to make some spot purchases.
The Exchange reported stales of Central Asian standards 1 and 2 and West African cotton for 1997 shipment.
Argentine medium grades traded for the fourth quarter, Israel-Acala through first quarter 1998 and Mexico-Juarez for second quarter 1997.
In extra long staples, the Exchange circulated offers from Sudan (Barakat) for the current quarter and from Israel (Pima) for second half 1997.
Cotton stocks as of May 15 totalled 36,007 bales, down from 131,628 bales a year earlier and compared with 41,504 a fortnight earlier.
